newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Cyclone in Australia shuts Wandoo oilfield.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Cyclone in Australia shuts Wandoo oilfield.

text.p: The Wandoo oil field offshore Western Australia was forced to shut-in production on Sunday due to a cyclone, the field's general manager, Ken Fitzpatrick said on Tuesday.
Production at a rate of about 10,000 barrels a day would resume as soon as the storm passes and anticipated high sea swells subside, Fitzpatrick told Reuters from Perth.
"We'll continue to monitor it (the cyclone) and be back in a couple of days," Fitzpatrick said.
The Wandoo field has recoverable reserves of about 75 million barrels and is operated by Mobil Corp unit, Ampolex Ltd.
The field produces a heavy crude with an American Petroleum Institute gravity of 19.4 percent.
The Bureau of Meterology said the cyclone, named Phil, has been downgraded to a Stage One category, meaning it no longer poses threats to coastal communities.
Waves generated by the cyclone were currently averaging between three and four metres in size, but dropping rapidly, a spokesman for the bureau said.
At 0100 GMT (12.00 noon), the storm was centered 380 km north of the the town of Karratha and moving west at 10 km an hour, the bureau said.
No other cyclones were forming in Australia, the bureau said.
Earlier on Tuesday, the operator of the 90,000-barrel-a-day Cossack-Pioneer oil platform, Woodside Petroleum Ltd, confirmed it had stopped production on Monday to avoid the cyclone.

Meanwhile, traders said another oil field in the path of the cyclone, located on Barrow Island, was continuing to produce crude but had suspended berthing activities with one tanker waiting to take on crude.
Officials of the operator of Barrow island, the West Australian Petroleum Pty Ltd (WAPET) consortium, were unavailable for comment.
WAPET is a joint venture of Texaco Inc, Chevron Inc and Royal Dutch/Shell Group, each with two-sevenths stakes, and Mobil, with one-seventh.
Barrow produces about 15,000 barrels of oil a day.
